docs.title: purecalendars
docs.text:
Holiday calendars and business-day arithmetic for Brazilian and US markets, computed offline.

purecalendars ships official holiday calendars for Brazil (ANBIMA, FEBRABAN, B3) and the United States (Federal Holidays), then layers a rich set of working-day / date helpers on top — is_working_day, add_working_days, working_days_range, delta_working_days, timezone-aware conversions, and more. Every calendar is computed locally: no network, no cache.

Live fetchers moved

The live fetchers (*Web classes, DatesUSNasdaq) moved to the separate opendata-calendars package, which returns purecalendars calendars.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: Section Description Usage Installation, choosing a provider, and basic examples Examples Task-oriented recipes (settlement dates, expiry, cross-market) API Reference Public providers and every shared calendar operation FAQ Common questions and troubleshooting Contributing Dev setup, testing, wheel build, PR workflow, releasing Changelog Per-version release history

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install purecalendars

from datetime import date

from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

cls_cal = DatesBRB3()
cls_cal.is_working_day(date(2024, 12, 25))          # False — Christmas
cls_cal.add_working_days(date(2024, 12, 24), 3)     # skips holidays + weekends
cls_cal.holidays()                                  # [(name, date), ...]

Everything works offline after install — no network, no browser.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Everything you need to develop, test, and release purecalendars.

See also: Usage · API Reference · the repository's CONTRIBUTING.md holds the authoritative branch/PR policy.

docs.title: Setting up for development
docs.text:
Clone the repo and bootstrap the environment. Every project command is a poe task, run through bash bin/poe_exec.sh <task>: the wrapper resolves poe from .venv first, so it works on the first run even when bin/venv.sh has just installed Poetry somewhere that is not on PATH yet.

git clone https://github.com/guilhermegor/purecalendars.git
cd purecalendars
bash bin/venv.sh                # create the Poetry venv and install deps (poe included)
bash bin/poe_exec.sh init       # seed .env, install pre-commit hooks

init composes three steps you can also run individually: ensure_env (seed .env from .env.example), venv (create the Poetry virtualenv and install all dependencies, including the dev tools), and precommit (install the git hooks). Poetry is auto-installed if missing.

Run bash bin/poe_exec.sh --help to list every task.

docs.title: Pre-commit hooks
docs.text:
bash bin/poe_exec.sh init installs the pre-commit hooks, which run automatically on every git commit and must pass before a commit is created. They mirror the CI gate (see below), so a clean local commit is a clean CI run. Run them on demand:

poetry run pre-commit run --all-files     # run every hook against the whole tree

If a formatting hook (e.g. ruff format) rewrites a file, the commit is aborted so you can review and re-stage the change — that is expected, just git add and commit again.

The shell linters (shellcheck, shfmt) install automatically with the dev dependencies — no extra step. bash bin/poe_exec.sh install_shell_linters exists only as an optional fallback for hosts where the pip-vendored binaries can't execute; you normally never need it.

docs.title: Running tests
docs.text:
bash bin/poe_exec.sh unit_tests         # unit tests only
bash bin/poe_exec.sh integration_tests  # integration tests only
bash bin/poe_exec.sh test_cov           # unit tests + coverage report + badge

purecalendars does no I/O, so unit tests never touch a real network, DB, or filesystem.

docs.title: The network guard
docs.text:
This is enforced, not merely expected. tests/conftest.py installs an autouse fixture that swaps the socket connection primitives (socket.socket.connect / connect_ex and socket.create_connection), so a test that reaches the wire fails immediately:

NetworkAccessError: A test tried to reach the network (...). Mock the I/O boundary
(the download / HTTP seam) instead, or mark the test @pytest.mark.allow_network if
it truly must hit the wire.

If you see this, something in purecalendars started doing I/O — which the package must not do (fetching belongs in opendata-calendars). Remove the I/O rather than work around the guard. A test that genuinely must hit the network opts out explicitly:

@pytest.mark.allow_network
def test_something_that_really_needs_the_wire() -> None: ...

Why it is a guard and not a guideline: purecalendars is a pure* package — computation only, no I/O. The guard turns that rule into a red test the moment network code creeps back in. Note that DNS resolution (socket.getaddrinfo) is deliberately not blocked: resolving an address neither exfiltrates data nor triggers a ban, and blocking it would break code that classifies an address before deciding whether to connect.

docs.title: The warning policy
docs.text: pytest.ini turns ResourceWarning, pytest.PytestUnraisableExceptionWarning and missing-docstring-parameter warnings into errors. DeprecationWarning, FutureWarning and UserWarning are no longer blanket-ignored: only the narrow, named filters in pytest.ini (PIL, matplotlib, beartype, numpy divide-by-zero) are silenced. Fix a new warning at its source; add a filter only with a reason.

docs.title: Linting and formatting
docs.text:
bash bin/poe_exec.sh lint   # ruff + mypy + codespell + pydocstyle + docstrings + shell/sql/yaml

Ruff config lives in ruff.toml, the BlueprintX template's (line-length 99, 4-space indent, double quotes, NumPy docstrings, preview mode on); read it for the active rule families and the deviations. bin/*.py is linted and formatted like src/ and tests/. Findings whose fix would change a signature or test strictness (PLR6301, PLR2004, PT011, ...) are baselined with an inline # noqa; remove one when you touch that code and can fix it properly. Docstring parameter/return types must match the type hints textually (int | float, not Union[int, float]) — the check-docstrings gate enforces this.

docs.title: Template provenance and drift
docs.text:
purecalendars was scaffolded from the BlueprintX lib-minimal template, and .blueprintx-provenance.yaml records which one: the tier, the BlueprintX version and commit (blueprintx_commit, the merge base for every comparison), the review-bot roster choice and the scaffold date. The stamp pins BlueprintX 12e76053 (v0.12.2): it was chosen by measurement as the commit whose template the vendored files match most (38 of the 47 comparable files byte for byte), not by date.

Two tools compare the project with a BlueprintX checkout. Both need one, passed as --blueprintx-root or exported as BLUEPRINTX_TEMPLATE_ROOT, and both run as poe tasks from the project root:

export BLUEPRINTX_TEMPLATE_ROOT=~/github/blueprintx   # or pass --blueprintx-root per call
bash bin/poe_exec.sh template_drift --root .          # report only; always exits 0
bash bin/poe_exec.sh template_update --root .         # dry run: lists what would change

check_template_drift.py classifies template-managed files as missing (the template ships it, the project lacks it), template changed since scaffold (the project left it alone) or both changed (the project edited it too). template_update.py is a dry run until --apply, which switches to chore/template-update-<short-sha>, merges with git merge-file and leaves the result uncommitted. Do not run --apply casually: it touches hundreds of files.

Known limits, recorded rather than fixed:

  • It reports only files the template still ships. A file the template dropped (docs/api.md) is not reported as removed here, because the stamped commit predates the --list-copies dry run the removed-file check needs (the run prints SKIPPED removed-file check).
  • Rendered files (README.md, pyproject.toml, LICENSE, SECURITY.md) and the bin/ci/ copies are outside the comparison.
  • The vendored package tree appears under the placeholder src/project/... in the template, not under src/purecalendars/....
  • The stamp keeps only the answers given at scaffold time (tier, roster choice, versions, commits); the other scaffold answers are not recorded.

A file the repository has since reformatted (ruff format, plus inline # noqa baselines) differs from the template byte for byte, so it shows up as changed on both sides without a real divergence.

docs.title: Building and verifying the wheel
docs.text:
Run this before your final commit / opening a PR. It builds the wheel, installs it into the Poetry environment, and smoke-imports the package — catching packaging mistakes (a missing __init__, an unshipped _internal/ subpackage, a broken public import) that source-tree tests never surface:

bash bin/poe_exec.sh install_dist_locally

A successful run prints Package import works followed by the version. If it fails, the wheel is broken even when unit_tests is green — fix it before pushing.

docs.title: Opening a branch and pull request
docs.text:
1. Branch off the default branch — main is protected, so never commit to it directly. Use a descriptive feat/…, fix/…, docs/…, chore/… name:

    git checkout -b feat/my-change

  2. Verify locally before pushing — the same gates CI runs:

    bash bin/poe_exec.sh unit_tests && bash bin/poe_exec.sh lint \
  && bash bin/poe_exec.sh install_dist_locally

  3. Open the PR. GitHub pre-fills the pull-request template; fill in every section — Description (what / why / how), Changes Made (added / updated / fixed), Testing (manual + automated evidence), Documentation, and Reviewer Focus. Link the issue the work addresses.

docs.title: The CI gate — must be green before review
docs.text:
Every push and pull request triggers the Run Tests workflow (.github/workflows/tests.yaml). A PR is only considered once all of these pass:

Gate What it checks codespell Spelling across the repo. docstring consistency pydocstyle (D412/D417) + check_docstrings.py — docstring types/raises match the signatures. ruff Lint + format (ruff check src/ tests/). mypy Static type check (cd src && mypy .). ignore_missing_imports = False: use a types-* stub where one exists, else add a [mypy-<pkg>.*] ignore section in mypy.ini. shell / sql / yaml lint Non-Python lint gates (mirrors the lint task). unit + integration tests The full pytest suites.

Because pre-commit mirrors these gates, a commit that passed your local hooks will pass CI.

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI (maintainers)
docs.text:
Two GitHub Actions workflows handle releases:

  • release-test-pypi.yaml — publish to Test PyPI first.
  • release-pypi.yaml — publish to PyPI and cut a GitHub release.

There is no manual version bump. The version is the git tag — pyproject.toml holds a 0.0.0 placeholder and poetry-dynamic-versioning stamps the real version at build time. To release, trigger the workflow from the Actions tab (workflow_dispatch) with the version (e.g. 1.1.0). The pipeline then:

  1. Runs the full test suite (tests.yaml, full matrix) as a hard gate — publishing is blocked unless tests pass on exactly this commit.
  2. Checks the version is greater than what is already published.
  3. Tags the commit v1.1.0, builds with python -m build (dynamic versioning stamps 1.1.0), and uploads via OIDC trusted publishing — no API token stored.
  4. Cuts a GitHub release for the tag. (Test PyPI builds the same version via POETRY_DYNAMIC_VERSIONING_BYPASS without creating a tag.)

Configure once:

  • A GitHub Environment per index (repository settings): release-pypi for PyPI, release-test-pypi for Test PyPI.
  • A trusted publisher on each index (PyPI and Test PyPI), matching this repo exactly: owner guilhermegor, repo purecalendars, workflow filename release-pypi.yaml (environment release-pypi) and release-test-pypi.yaml (environment release-test-pypi). On a first-ever release use a pending publisher (register it before the project exists). No PYPI_TOKEN / TEST_PYPI_TOKEN secret is needed.

Documentation is published separately — every push to main runs .github/workflows/docs.yaml, which builds this site and deploys it to GitHub Pages.

docs.title: Changelog (maintainers)
docs.text: CHANGELOG.md is generated from the conventional-commit history and the git tags, never committed to main by CI. The published site's Changelog page is regenerated fresh on every docs build (docs.yaml runs cz changelog before mkdocs build), and each release also gets GitHub-generated release notes. This keeps branch protection intact and needs no stored secret (no PAT, no bypass). The only discipline is writing feat: / fix: / etc. commit messages; preview the changelog locally any time with bash bin/poe_exec.sh changelog.

docs.title: Examples & Recipes
docs.text:
Task-oriented snippets for common date/holiday problems. Each is self-contained.

See also: Usage for the basics · API Reference for every method.

docs.title: Compute a T+N settlement date
docs.text:
Advance a trade date by N business days on the B3 exchange calendar:

from datetime import date

from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

cls_cal = DatesBRB3()
trade_date = date(2024, 12, 20)
settlement = cls_cal.add_working_days(trade_date, 2)   # T+2, skipping weekends + holidays
print(settlement)

docs.title: Roll a due date off a holiday/weekend
docs.text:
Snap a nominal due date to the next (or previous) business day:

from datetime import date

from purecalendars.br.anbima import DatesBRAnbima

cls_cal = DatesBRAnbima()
due = date(2025, 1, 1)                                  # New Year — a holiday
print(cls_cal.nearest_working_day(due, bool_next=True))  # first business day on/after
print(cls_cal.nearest_working_day(due, bool_next=False)) # last business day on/before

docs.title: Count business days between two dates
docs.text:
E.g. an SLA or aging metric in working days:

from datetime import date

from purecalendars.us.federal_holidays import DatesUSFederalHolidays

cls_cal = DatesUSFederalHolidays()
opened = date(2024, 12, 20)
closed = date(2025, 1, 6)
print(cls_cal.delta_working_days(opened, closed))   # business days elapsed

docs.title: Find options expiry (3rd Friday of a month)
docs.text:
from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

cls_cal = DatesBRB3()
# weekday: Monday=0 … Friday=4; n=3 → the third Friday, rolled to a working day if needed.
expiry = cls_cal.get_nth_weekday_month(2025, 3, weekday=4, n=3)
print(expiry)

docs.title: List every holiday in a year
docs.text:
from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

cls_cal = DatesBRB3()
for name, day in sorted(cls_cal.holidays(), key=lambda pair: pair[1]):
    if day.year == 2025:
        print(day, name)

docs.title: Build a working-day set for fast membership tests
docs.text:
from datetime import date

from purecalendars.br.febraban import DatesBRFebraban

cls_cal = DatesBRFebraban()
business_days = cls_cal.working_days_range(date(2025, 1, 1), date(2025, 3, 31))
print(date(2025, 2, 17) in business_days)   # O(1) lookup against the quarter

docs.title: Cross-market: is it a working day in both BR and the US?
docs.text:
from datetime import date

from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3
from purecalendars.us.federal_holidays import DatesUSFederalHolidays

cls_br = DatesBRB3()
cls_us = DatesUSFederalHolidays()

def is_dual_working_day(day: date) -> bool:
    """True only when both the B3 and US federal calendars are open."""
    return cls_br.is_working_day(day) and cls_us.is_working_day(day)

print(is_dual_working_day(date(2025, 7, 4)))   # US Independence Day → False

docs.title: FAQ & Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Common questions and fixes when using purecalendars.

See also: Usage · API Reference

docs.title: Where did DatesBRB3Web, DatesUSNasdaq and the other live fetchers go?
docs.text: They moved to the separate opendata-calendars package in 3.0.0. purecalendars does no I/O: every provider here is computed offline, with no network, no cache and no browser. opendata-calendars fetches the publishers' live tables and returns them as purecalendars calendars.

docs.title: Why does a US federal holiday show up on both a Sunday and the next Monday?
docs.text: That is correct and intentional. DatesUSFederalHolidays follows the federal observed-day rule (5 U.S.C. §6103): when a holiday lands on a weekend, the observed closure day is emitted in addition to the statutory date — a Saturday holiday is observed the preceding Friday, a Sunday holiday the following Monday. So for 2023, New Year's Day appears on Sun 1 Jan (statutory) and Mon 2 Jan (observed). Nothing is moved or hidden; the Monday is added because federal offices, banks, and markets are genuinely closed then — and is_working_day(Mon 2 Jan) must return False for correct business-day math. Brazilian calendars have no such rule and keep each holiday on its published date.

docs.title: Can a holiday be stale?
docs.text: Not in the cache sense: every provider recomputes from statutory rules on every call, so there is nothing to refresh. A calendar can only be wrong when a publisher declares an extraordinary closure the rules do not know; add it yourself (see below) until a release picks it up.

docs.title: ZoneInfoNotFoundError on a timezone lookup
docs.text:
purecalendars depends on tzdata so the IANA timezone database is available even on systems that ship none (notably Windows and minimal containers). If you see this error, confirm tzdata installed alongside the package:

pip show tzdata

docs.title: Which provider should I use for trading-day logic?
docs.text:
• Brazilian exchange (B3): DatesBRB3 — national holidays plus B3 non-trading days, including 24 December, which B3 publishes as a closure (pass bool_add_christmas_eve=False to opt out; the default changed in 2.0).
  • Brazilian banking / settlement: DatesBRFebraban.
  • US market: DatesUSFederalHolidays is the civil federal-holiday calendar, not the exchange's. Nasdaq market closures (e.g. Good Friday) come from opendata-calendars.

See the provider comparison table for what each one loads.

docs.title: Can I add my own one-off holidays?
docs.text:
Yes — every provider inherits add_holidays:

from datetime import date
from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

cls_cal = DatesBRB3()
cls_cal.add_holidays([("Company offsite", date(2025, 6, 2))])

docs.title: Incident Records
docs.text:
What broke in this project, and what changed so it cannot break that way again. This page keeps debugging knowledge inside the codebase instead of in git history and one person's memory — the knowledge a team already paid for once should not have to be paid for twice.

See also: Usage · Contributing · Changelog.

docs.title: Not an ADR, and not a lessons store
docs.text:
An ADR records a decision made before something went wrong. An incident record documents one made because something already did — different trigger, different audience. If this project adopts ADRs later, keep the two separate rather than merging them into one grab-bag.

This is also not a copy of a scaffolding tool's own "lessons learned" store. That kind of store answers "what should every future generated project inherit" — this page answers "what bit this codebase, and what did we do about it." Different audience, different lifetime.

docs.title: Published on purpose — redact before you write
docs.text: This page ships in the published docs site, same as Usage. An incident can carry production detail (a hostname, a query, a customer-facing symptom) that should not reach a public site — redact or generalize it before committing the entry, the way an external postmortem omits internal specifics. If this project's site is genuinely public and entries cannot stay redacted, exclude incidents.md via exclude_docs in mkdocs.yml instead of leaving it half-written.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
Five fields, in this order. Keep each to a few sentences — the entry stops getting written the day it takes an hour to fill in.

  • Symptom — what was observed, not what was wrong.
  • How it was found — the tool, command, or accident that surfaced it; "we were careful" does not belong here.
  • Root cause — measured, not assumed.
  • The change — what now makes this class of failure impossible, or loud instead of silent.
  • How we'd know it regressed — the gate, test, or assertion that would catch it coming back.

No incidents recorded yet. Add the first entry below this line, newest first.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Installing and using purecalendars.

See also: API Reference for the full method list · Contributing to develop or release the library.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install purecalendars

Or with Poetry:

poetry add purecalendars

Everything works offline after install — no network, no browser.

docs.title: Choosing a provider
docs.text:
Every provider exposes the same calendar-operations surface (see API Reference); they differ only in which holidays they load.

Every provider is computed offline. For the publishers' own live tables, use the separate opendata-calendars package.

from purecalendars.br.anbima import DatesBRAnbima      # ANBIMA national holidays
from purecalendars.br.febraban import DatesBRFebraban  # FEBRABAN bank holidays
from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3              # national + B3 exchange extras
from purecalendars.us.federal_holidays import DatesUSFederalHolidays  # US federal holidays

You can also import from the country package:

from purecalendars.br import DatesBRAnbima, DatesBRB3, DatesBRFebraban
from purecalendars.us import DatesUSFederalHolidays

docs.title: Working with business days
docs.text:
from datetime import date

from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

cls_cal = DatesBRB3()

cls_cal.is_working_day(date(2024, 12, 25))   # False — Christmas
cls_cal.is_holiday(date(2024, 12, 25))       # True
cls_cal.is_weekend(date(2024, 12, 28))       # True — Saturday

# Add three business days, skipping weekends and holidays.
cls_cal.add_working_days(date(2024, 12, 24), 3)     # -> date(2024, 12, 30)

# Nearest business day on or after (or before) a given date.
cls_cal.nearest_working_day(date(2024, 12, 25), bool_next=True)

# Count / list business days in a range.
cls_cal.delta_working_days(date(2024, 12, 1), date(2024, 12, 31))
cls_cal.working_days_range(date(2024, 12, 1), date(2024, 12, 31))

DatesBRB3 here is just an example — the same methods work on every provider (DatesBRAnbima, DatesBRFebraban, DatesUSFederalHolidays); only the loaded holiday set differs. See the API Reference for the full list of classes and their shared methods.

docs.title: Listing holidays
docs.text:
Every provider returns (name, date) tuples:

from purecalendars.us.federal_holidays import DatesUSFederalHolidays

for name, day in DatesUSFederalHolidays().holidays():
    print(day, name)

docs.text:
The public interface, grouped by the code's own top-level split: one class per provider module under a two-letter country package (purecalendars.<country>.<provider>).

See also: Usage

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Group Contents Reference Every country provider (Brazil, United States) and the shared calendar operations they inherit

docs.title: Growing this section
docs.text:
This is a directory, not a single page, on purpose. An API reference grows once per shipped unit, so a single api.md becomes the largest page in the repo; splitting it later is trivial effort but rots every published deep link — and permanently, once versioned docs are live, because /<version>/api/#anchor exists forever. The premium for starting as a directory is one extra file and one nav level, paid once.

When you add pages:

  • Group by the codebase's own top-level split — never invent a parallel taxonomy (e.g. one page per country package, mirroring the package's own split). A reader who knows the package can then guess the URL, and the docs cannot drift from a structure they mirror.
  • Depth follows count, not taste. The real axis picks the sections; volume alone decides whether a section needs a second level.
  • Prose shared by one group lives once on that group's page, not restated per item.
  • Register every new page in mkdocs.yml nav: in the same commit. MkDocs builds an unregistered page anyway — it just vanishes from navigation, which is how a page silently goes missing.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
Complete public interface for purecalendars.

See also: Usage

The public API is the set of country providers, one class per module under a two-letter country package (purecalendars.<country>.<provider>). Every provider loads a different holiday calendar but shares the same date-operations surface — the shared calendar operations documented at the bottom of this page.

Every provider is computed offline — no network, no cache. Live fetchers of the publishers' own tables live in the separate opendata-calendars package.

Provider Import Holidays it loads DatesBRAnbima purecalendars.br.anbima Brazilian national holidays (ANBIMA) DatesBRFebraban purecalendars.br.febraban Brazilian bank holidays (FEBRABAN) DatesBRB3 purecalendars.br.b3 National + B3 exchange non-trading days DatesUSFederalHolidays purecalendars.us.federal_holidays US federal public holidays

docs.title: Constructor parameters
docs.text: Every provider computes its holidays locally, so the constructors take only int_year_start, int_year_end, and an optional logger (plus bool_add_christmas_eve for DatesBRB3).

docs.title: Brazil — purecalendars.br
docs.text:
Why the offline BR calendars use holidays.B3

The offline Brazilian providers are computed from holidays.B3 (Brasil, Bolsa, Balcão), not holidays.Brazil. The latter is the statutory-only national set and omits Carnaval (Monday and Tuesday) and Corpus Christi — neither is a statutory national holiday, but banks and markets close on both. Using it would silently mark Carnaval as a working day.

The equivalence was verified before the default was switched: over the full 2001–2099 span ANBIMA publishes, the offline set and the fetched workbook have an empty symmetric difference. The same holds for FEBRABAN (checked against its live endpoint for 2025–2026) and for B3 once its last-working-day-of-year rule is applied.

docs.title: DatesBRAnbima
docs.text:
The ANBIMA calendar — computed offline, no network.

from purecalendars.br.anbima import DatesBRAnbima

DatesBRAnbima(
    int_year_start=2001, int_year_end=2099,   # defaults: ANBIMA's full published span
    logger=None,
)

Holidays: the Brazilian national holiday set published by ANBIMA — Confraternização Universal (New Year), Carnaval, Sexta-feira Santa (Good Friday), Tiradentes, Dia do Trabalho, Corpus Christi, Independência, Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Finados, Proclamação da República, Consciência Negra, Natal.

Source: the holidays package (offline computation). No cache parameters — there is nothing to fetch.

Provider-specific methods: none beyond the shared surface; holidays() returns the computed (name, date) list.

docs.title: DatesBRFebraban
docs.text:
The FEBRABAN calendar — computed offline, no network.

from purecalendars.br.febraban import DatesBRFebraban

DatesBRFebraban(
    int_year_start=2025, int_year_end=2026,   # defaults: last year and this year
    logger=None,
)

Holidays: Brazilian bank holidays (bank non-working days) for the requested int_year_start…int_year_end range.

Source: the holidays package (offline computation). FEBRABAN has no dedicated entry in that package, but its published federal bank holidays were verified identical to holidays.B3 for 2025 and 2026; years outside that window follow the same statutory rules but have not been diffed against FEBRABAN's own publication.

Provider-specific methods: none beyond the shared surface.

docs.title: DatesBRB3
docs.text:
The B3 calendar — computed offline, no network.

from purecalendars.br.b3 import DatesBRB3

DatesBRB3(
    bool_add_christmas_eve=True,              # 24 Dec is a non-trading day (default)
    int_year_start=2001, int_year_end=2099,
    logger=None,
)

Holidays: the national set plus the B3 exchange's own non-trading days — the last working day of each year, and 24 December (Christmas Eve). Use this provider for trading-day logic on the Brazilian exchange.

bool_add_christmas_eve defaults to True because B3's published calendar carries 24 December as a closure ("não haverá negociação") in every year it falls on a weekday — verified live for 2021, 2024, 2025 and 2026. Pass False to restore the pre-2.0 behaviour, in which the offline calendar omitted the date and therefore disagreed with the exchange.

Changed in 2.0

The default was False up to and including 1.0.1, so DatesBRB3() used to report 24 December as a working day. If you depend on that, pass bool_add_christmas_eve=False explicitly. The date is added unconditionally, so in a year where 24 December falls on a weekend it appears in the holiday list even though B3 omits it — harmless for working-day arithmetic, since a weekend is already non-working.

Source: the holidays package + B3 exchange rules (offline computation).

Provider-specific methods:

Method Signature Returns Description holidays_to_add (set_dates_national) list[tuple[str, date]] The extra (name, date) pairs B3 adds beyond the national set. get_last_working_day (int_year, set_dates_national) date The year's last non-weekend, non-holiday day. get_christmas_eve (int_year) date 24 December of int_year (added unless bool_add_christmas_eve=False).

docs.title: DatesUSFederalHolidays
docs.text:
The US federal calendar — computed offline, no network and no browser.

from purecalendars.us.federal_holidays import DatesUSFederalHolidays

DatesUSFederalHolidays(
    int_year_start=2024, int_year_end=2025,   # year range to compute
    logger=None,
)

Holidays: the eleven US federal public holidays for the requested year range (New Year's, MLK, Washington's Birthday, Memorial, Juneteenth, Independence, Labor, Columbus, Veterans, Thanksgiving, Christmas), computed from their statutory rules via the holidays package.

Observed-day rule (5 U.S.C. §6103). When a holiday falls on a weekend, the observed federal closure day is also emitted: a Saturday holiday is observed the preceding Friday, a Sunday holiday the following Monday. Both the statutory date and the observed date are returned — e.g. for 2023, New Year's Day appears on Sunday 1 Jan and the observed closure on Monday 2 Jan. Nothing is hidden or moved; the Monday is added because federal offices, banks, and markets are genuinely closed then, which is required for correct working-day math.

Source: the holidays package (offline computation). No cache parameters — there is nothing to fetch, so the constructor takes only the year range and an optional logger.

Provider-specific methods: none beyond the shared surface; holidays() returns the computed (name, date) list.

docs.title: Shared calendar operations
docs.text:
Every provider inherits all of the methods below — they are canonical to each calendar class. They come from a linear chain of internal capability mixins that build up the ABCCalendarOperations facade every provider extends:

ABCCalendar → CalendarCore → DateManipulation → DateTimezoneAware
            → DatesRangeDelta → DatesCurrent → DateFormatter → ABCCalendarOperations

Each layer below lists the methods it contributes. Throughout, date_ accepts either a date or a datetime.

docs.title: Holidays & working-day predicates — CalendarCore
docs.text: Method Signature Returns Description holidays () list[tuple[str, date]] Every holiday the provider loads, as (name, date) pairs — the base set all working-day logic builds on. holidays_in_year (int_year) list[int] Day-of-year ordinals that fall on a holiday in int_year; handy for fast membership checks. is_holiday (date_) bool Whether the date is a loaded holiday. Gate settlement / trading logic on this. is_weekend (date_) bool Whether the date is a Saturday or Sunday. is_working_day (date_) bool The core business-day test — True when the date is neither weekend nor holiday. date_only (date_) date Normalise a datetime to its date, dropping the time; used before day arithmetic. get_holidays_raw (timeout=(12.0, 21.0)) DataFrame The untransformed upstream holiday table — for debugging or custom pipelines.

docs.title: Date manipulation — DateManipulation
docs.text: Method Signature Returns Description add_holidays (list_new_holidays) None Inject extra (name, date) holidays at runtime — e.g. a one-off company closure on top of the official set. add_working_days (date_, int_days_to_add) date Advance by N business days, skipping weekends + holidays (negative N goes back). The T+N settlement primitive. add_calendar_days (date_, int_days_to_add) date Add N calendar days, ignoring weekends/holidays. add_months (date_, int_months_to_add) datetime Add N calendar months, preserving day-of-month where valid. nearest_working_day (date_, bool_next=True) date Snap a date to the nearest business day — forward by default, backward with bool_next=False. Rolls a due date off a holiday. build_date (year, month, day) date Construct a date from components. build_datetime (year, month, day, hour, minute, second, str_timezone="UTC") datetime Construct a timezone-aware datetime from components. str_date_to_date (str_date, format_input="DD/MM/YYYY") date Parse a date string using a format token (e.g. "YYYY-MM-DD") into a date. timestamp_to_date (timestamp_, substr_timestamp="T") date Parse a timestamp string into a date, splitting on substr_timestamp. timestamp_to_datetime (timestamp_, substr_timestamp="T") datetime Parse a timestamp string into a datetime. excel_float_to_date (numeric_excel_date) date Convert an Excel serial number to a date (handles the 1900 leap-year bug). to_integer (date_) int Encode a date as a YYYYMMDD integer — a compact sortable key for storage/comparison.

docs.title: Timezone & timestamp conversion — DateTimezoneAware
docs.text: Method Signature Returns Description change_timezone (date_, target_tz="UTC", source_tz=None) datetime Re-express a date/datetime in target_tz; pass source_tz for naive inputs. date_to_datetime (date_, str_timezone="UTC") datetime Promote a date to a midnight datetime in the given timezone. str_date_to_datetime (str_date, format_input="DD/MM/YYYY", str_timezone="UTC") datetime Parse a date string to a timezone-aware datetime. to_unix_timestamp (date_, str_timezone="UTC") int Convert a date / datetime / time to Unix epoch seconds. iso_to_unix_timestamp (iso_timestamp, str_timezone="UTC") int Convert an ISO-8601 string to Unix epoch seconds. unix_timestamp_to_date (unix_timestamp, str_timezone="UTC") date Convert Unix epoch seconds back to a date in the given timezone. unix_timestamp_to_datetime (unix_timestamp, str_timezone="UTC") datetime Convert Unix epoch seconds back to a datetime. excel_float_to_datetime (float_date, str_timezone="UTC") datetime Convert an Excel serial number to a timezone-aware datetime, including the fractional-day time.

docs.title: Ranges & deltas — DatesRangeDelta
docs.text: Method Signature Returns Description working_days_range (date_start, date_end) set[date] All business days within [start, end] inclusive. calendar_days_range (date_start, date_end) set[date] All calendar days within [start, end] inclusive. delta_working_days (date_start, date_end) int Count of business days between two dates — e.g. SLA / aging in business days. delta_calendar_days (date_start, date_end) int Count of calendar days between two dates. delta_working_hours (timestamp_start, timestamp_end, …office/lunch hours…) int Business hours between two timestamps, honouring configurable office + lunch windows and holidays. get_dates_weekday_month (year, month, weekday) list[date] Every occurrence of a given weekday in a month (e.g. all Mondays). get_last_working_day_years (list_years) list[date] The last business day of each requested year — for year-end processing. get_nth_weekday_month (year, month, weekday, n, bool_working_days=True, bool_next_working_day=True) date The n-th given weekday of a month (e.g. 3rd Wednesday — options expiry), optionally rolled to a working day. get_start_end_day_month (date_, bool_working_days=False) tuple[date, date] The first and last day of a date's month, optionally as working days. years_between_dates (date_start, date_end) set[int] The set of calendar years a range spans.

docs.title: Current date & time — DatesCurrent
docs.text: Method Signature Returns Description curr_date () date Today's date. curr_datetime (str_timezone="UTC") datetime The current datetime in the given timezone. curr_time (str_timezone="UTC") time The current time-of-day in the given timezone. current_timestamp_string (format_output="%Y%m%d_%H%M%S", str_timezone="UTC") str The current timestamp formatted as a string — handy for filenames / log keys.

docs.title: Formatting & components — DateFormatter
docs.text: Method Signature Returns Description day_number (date_) int Day of month (1–31). week_number (date_) str ISO week number. month_number (date_, bool_month_mm=False) int \| str Month as an int, or a zero-padded "MM" string when bool_month_mm=True. month_name (date_, bool_abbreviation=False, str_timezone="UTC") str Locale-aware month name (full, or abbreviated when bool_abbreviation=True). month_str (date_) str Month rendered as a string. year_number (date_) int Four-digit year. weekday_name (date_, bool_abbreviation=False, str_timezone="UTC") str Locale-aware weekday name (full, or abbreviated when bool_abbreviation=True). get_platform_locale (str_locale=None, str_timezone=None) str Resolve a platform-appropriate locale string backing the name methods above. utc_log_ts () datetime A UTC datetime intended for log timestamps.

docs.title: Subclassing ABCCalendarOperations
docs.text:
ABCCalendarOperations is public: from purecalendars import ABCCalendarOperations. Subclass it to build a calendar of your own and inherit every method above.

Override to supply holidays. _source_holidays(self) -> list[tuple[str, date]] — the (name, date) pairs of your calendar. Its default returns [] and nothing is abstract, so a subclass that omits or misspells it raises nothing and has weekends as its only non-working days.

May override. get_holidays_raw(timeout) — returns an empty DataFrame (name, date columns) by default; override it to expose an upstream table.

Should not override. holidays() — it returns _source_holidays() plus the holidays added through add_holidays, so overriding it drops those additions.

May rely on.

  • holidays() and the whole surface (is_holiday, is_working_day, add_working_days, ...) reading the calendar through _source_holidays; weekends are non-working on top of it.
  • add_holidays working even when your __init__ does not call super().__init__().

Must not assume. That _source_holidays is re-read on every call: the date set behind is_holiday and is_working_day is built on first use and refreshed only by add_holidays, so fix your configuration (for example a year range) before the first query.

from datetime import date

from purecalendars import ABCCalendarOperations


class DatesXX(ABCCalendarOperations):
    def _source_holidays(self) -> list[tuple[str, date]]:
        return [("New Year", date(2026, 1, 1))]

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Convention Rule Public API ABCCalendarOperations from the package root; country providers under purecalendars.<cc>.<provider>, one class per module. Private code Everything under purecalendars._internal is off-limits — internal, may change. Type hints Required on all public methods, including -> None returns. Docstrings NumPy style; explain why, not what.
